scope: Artwork is theological visual interpretation at its historical production date, not a documentary view of Genesis episodes or of the 1962 Mass.

artworks.title: San Vitale — Abel and Melchizedek at one altar
artworks.interpretiveFunction: Sixth-century explicitly Eucharistic Christian typological juxtaposition of two biblical figures at one altar, visually developed long before the modern painted scenes. Does not depict a common meeting of Abel and Melchizedek in biblical history.

historicalEvidence.role: Regional heritage object record (primary museum catalogue)
historicalEvidence.attests: VI-century mosaic 540–547: Abel with lamb and Melchizedek with bread at common altar; explicitly anachronistic typological grouping.
Basilica San Vitale and biblical offering iconography in the presbytery.

artworks.title: Sant'Apollinare in Classe — Abel, Melchizedek and Abraham
artworks.dateRange: seventh-century panel, extensively restored in eighteenth century
artworks.interpretiveFunction: Rare premodern artwork placing all three persons explicitly named in the Roman Canon within a single Christian Eucharistic iconographic statement. The three biblical episodes did not occur together.

historicalEvidence.role: Italian Ministry of Culture museum site
historicalEvidence.attests: Right-side apse panel interprets Eucharistic sacrifice through Abel, Melchizedek and Abraham, dates to seventh century and was much restored.

historicalEvidence.role: Dictionnaire de théologie catholique, Abel article
historicalEvidence.attests: Early Christian iconography connected Abel and Melchizedek; attribution to individual ancient artistic sources needs careful object-by-object verification.

artworks.title: Late antique Christian sarcophagi — Cain and Abel offerings
artworks.dateRange: multiple historic periods; object-by-object certification required
artworks.interpretiveFunction: Later Christian funerary art used Abel and Cain's offerings symbolically in relation to the Eucharist. This is historiography of devotional iconography; no one exact ancient piece, date or GPS location is established by the dictionary article.

historicalEvidence.role: Dictionnaire de théologie catholique, article Abel
historicalEvidence.attests: Documents variant readings of Cain/Abel sarcophagus iconography, warns that identifying divine acceptance/rejection solely from schematic drawings is problematic.
